mechanism_narrative: A lower current federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) predicts positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns, as lower rates reduce the discount rate applied to equity cash flows, increasing present value of future earnings.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when FEDFUNDS is below the 50th percentile of its historical range (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeds 4.5%, it signals a deteriorating labor market that may lead to economic contraction, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE > 4.5% (p-value > 0.05 for negative return rate).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and industrial production (INDPRO) indicates a broad-based economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where both HOUST and INDPRO decline (p-value > 0.05 for negative return rate).

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle, a rise in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) signals accelerating inflation, prompting the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates, which depresses equity valuations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during monetary tightening cycles when CPIAUCSL rises (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A higher current real GDP level (GDPC1) predicts positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns, as it reflects a strong economic expansion supporting corporate earnings growth.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when GDPC1 is above its 10-year moving average (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the level of nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) falls below 145,000 (thousands), it signals a weakening labor market, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where PAYEMS < 145000 (p-value > 0.05 for negative return rate).

mechanism_narrative: During periods of stable or declining federal funds rates (FEDFUNDS) and rising retail sales (RSAFS), strong consumer demand without monetary tightening supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when RSAFS rises and FEDFUNDS is stable or declining (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During a supply shock regime, a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals reduced economic output, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during supply shock regimes when INDPRO declines (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
